## Discovery & Translational Science

- **A decade of progress translating base editors into clinical development** [Nature Reviews Drug Discovery](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41573-026-01548-7)
  - Comprehensive review tracing 10 years of base editing evolution from initial bench discovery to clinical translation.
  - Highlights ongoing engineering advances to minimize bystander editing, improve targeting scope, and streamline in vivo lipid nanoparticle delivery.
  - Details current clinical trial landscape across hematologic, metabolic, and genetic disorders.

- **Biopharma ADC pipeline analysis highlights top targets ahead of ESMO 2026** [X / Twitter](https://x.com/JacobPlieth/status/2111177202436100337)
  - Industry analysis highlights over 50 antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) scheduled for presentation at ESMO 2026, categorized by payload chemistry and antigen target.
  - B7-H3-targeted topoisomerase I inhibitor (TOPO1i) payloads lead development momentum, with 7 distinct clinical-stage constructs under evaluation.

- **Multimodal biomarker profiling identifies drivers of primary anti-PD-(L)1 resistance in NSCLC** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.01.09.26343779)
  - Prospective, multicenter PIONeeR study evaluated 439 advanced NSCLC patients receiving first-line chemo-immunotherapy or second-line anti-PD-(L)1 monotherapy across six biological layers.
  - Evaluated 360 machine learning pipelines using transcriptomics, genomics, high-dimensional circulating immune phenotyping, soluble vascular markers, and multiplex digital pathology.
  - Developed predictive signatures to prospectively identify patients at high risk of primary resistance to immune checkpoint blockade.

- **Engineered iPSC-derived APCs secreting IL-12 enable off-the-shelf cancer immunotherapy** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/4288850/)
  - Preclinical study demonstrates that human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived antigen-presenting cells (iPSC-APCs) engineered to produce IL-12 enhance T-cell and NK-cell activation.
  - Engineered allogeneic cells sustained localized IL-12 secretion, remodeling the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment without inducing systemic toxicity in model systems.

- **Plasma pTau217 demonstrates superior 11-year dementia prediction over blood NfL** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.10.15.26365615)
  - Longitudinal HUNT study analysis (n = 3,935; follow-up 11 years) showed plasma phosphorylated tau217 (pTau217) plus demographic factors predicted all-cause dementia with an AUC of 0.773 (95% CI: 0.756–0.790).
  - Adding multimodal risk scores yielded minor predictive gains (AUC 0.775–0.783), while adding neurofilament light chain (NfL) provided no significant improvement.
  - Stratification revealed higher predictive accuracy in APOE4-positive individuals (AUC 0.811–0.820) and a 5- to 11-fold increase in dementia odds for the highest combined risk tertile.

- **Surgical-only esophageal adenocarcinoma cohort identifies key genomic prognostic markers** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.10.14.26365576)
  - Genomic profiling using a 451-gene panel in 65 treatment-naive esophageal adenocarcinoma patients undergoing surgical resection (median follow-up > 11 years) established baseline prognostic mutations unconfounded by perioperative chemo-radiation.
  - Worse overall survival was significantly linked to gene amplifications in *CCND1* (HR = 3.08, p = 0.02) and *EGFR* (HR = 2.98, p = 0.01), loss of *ARID2* (HR = 2.12, p = 0.05), and missense mutations in *RYR1* (HR = 2.68, p = 0.01).

- **LUCID platform leverages single-cell SRS imaging and AI for early bladder cancer detection** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.10.14.26365504)
  - Integrated single-cell stimulated Raman scattering (SRS) microscopy platform analyzed lipid and protein distribution across 19,678 exfoliated urinary cells from 26 bladder cancer patients and 54 non-cancer controls.
  - Automated feature extraction combined with a multiple-instance learning XGBoost model achieved non-invasive detection of bladder cancer by profiling intracellular lipid droplet dynamics.

- **GPU-accelerated RhythmWriter platform enables high-throughput cardiac safety screening** [bioRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.10.15.759435)
  - Open-source ImageJ plugin quantifies prolonged contractile motion and restitution dynamics in human iPSC-derived cardiomyocyte (hiPSC-CM) aggregates.
  - RW accurately captured rapid electrical entrainment down to 245 ms cycle lengths and S2 refractory beats down to 130 ms, enabling automated high-throughput contractility and cardiotoxicity screening.

- **Translational target validation of Factor XI and XII inhibition in acute ischemic stroke** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42888464/)
  - Review synthesizes preclinical data and emerging clinical trial results for Factor XI (FXI) and Factor XII (FXII) targeted inhibitors in ischemic stroke.
  - Evaluated contact system inhibition as a therapeutic strategy to prevent thrombosis without disrupting primary hemostasis or increasing intracranial hemorrhage risk.

## Early Trials — Phase I–II

- **[Biotech]** **Imeglimin shows efficacy and safety in Phase 2 IMELD trial for MASLD with type 2 diabetes** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42888537/)
  - Single-center, single-arm Phase 2 trial evaluated oral imeglimin hydrochloride, a novel oxidative phosphorylation fixer, in patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and T2D.
  - Achieved study endpoints for hepatic safety, glycemic control, and reduction of liver fat accumulation over the treatment period.

- **High-capacity 6 mA tDCS demonstrates rapid antidepressant activity in Phase 1 pilot** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.10.05.26364655)
  - Open-label pilot trial evaluated accelerated high-capacity transcranial direct current stimulation (HC-tDCS) at 6 mA delivered twice daily over 5 days (20 sessions total) in 20 patients with major depressive disorder.
  - Completed with 100% session retention (203/203 sessions); mean PHQ-9 depression scores decreased from 15.8 to 7.2 (Hedges g = 1.62), with 50% achieving clinical remission at day 5.
  - Transient burning (46%), electrode-site erythema (100%), and minor residual post-inflammatory skin pigmentation at 1 month (10%, Black participants) were noted without serious adverse events.

- **Phase 2 crossover trial measures cannabidiol oil effects on auditory MMN in pediatric autism** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.10.14.26365371)
  - Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover study (n = 19, ages 6–12) assessed 12 weeks of oral CBD oil on electrophysiological duration-deviant mismatch negativity (MMN).
  - CBD trended toward shortening peak MMN latency at the FCz electrode site relative to placebo, though the interaction did not achieve significance following false discovery rate correction (p = 0.029, pFDR = 0.058).

- **⁶⁸Ga-Pentixafor PET/MRI localizes corticotroph adenomas in Cushing disease pilot** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42888349/)
  - Pilot clinical imaging trial evaluated CXCR4-targeted ⁶⁸Ga-Pentixafor PET/MRI in patients with ACTH-dependent Cushing disease.
  - Non-invasive molecular imaging accurately detected microadenomas, demonstrating utility for preoperative pituitary lesion localization.

## Late & Pivotal Trials — Phase III

- **[Big Pharma]** **Re-analysis of Phase 3 LITESPARK-022 trial shows attenuation of belzutifan benefit after treatment completion** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.10.14.26365591)
  - Reconstructed individual patient data from the Phase 3 LITESPARK-022 trial evaluating adjuvant belzutifan plus pembrolizumab versus pembrolizumab alone in clear cell renal cell carcinoma (RCC).
  - Hazard ratio for disease-free survival (DFS) was 0.55 (95% CI: 0.43–0.71) during the 1-year treatment phase, but shifted to 1.16 (95% CI: 0.87–1.54) after therapy stopped.
  - The 24-month restricted mean survival time difference was 1.34 months, showing early benefit attenuation similar to historical adjuvant tyrosine kinase inhibitor trials.

- **[Big Pharma]** **Phase 3 exit interviews characterize patient preference for oral GLP-1 orforglipron over oral semaglutide** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42888373/)
  - Qualitative patient exit interviews conducted alongside a Phase 3 head-to-head trial comparing Eli Lilly's once-daily non-peptide oral GLP-1 agonist orforglipron to Novo Nordisk's oral semaglutide in type 2 diabetes.
  - Participants reported improved satisfaction regarding administration flexibility and daily dosing logistics without rigid food and water fasting restrictions.

- **[Big Pharma]** **Post hoc Phase 3 analysis quantifies brexpiprazole effects on agitation domains in Alzheimer's dementia** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42888370/)
  - Post hoc analysis of pivotal Phase 3 trials evaluated caregiver-reported outcomes for brexpiprazole (Rexulti) across specific behavioral subdomains in Alzheimer's dementia.
  - Treatment yielded consistent, domain-specific reductions in aggressive behavior, verbal agitation, and physical restlessness compared to placebo.

## Regulatory & Approvals

- **[Biotech]** **Revolution Medicines' pancreatic cancer therapy Rasonque recommended for EU approval** [STAT+](https://www.statnews.com/2026/10/16/biotech-news-revmed-pancreatic-cancer-drug-nears-european-approval/?utm_campaign=rss)
  - European Medicines Agency CHMP issued a positive opinion recommending approval of Revolution Medicines' RAS inhibitor Rasonque for advanced pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma.
  - Decision follows prior US FDA approval for the targeted oncology candidate.

- **[Big Pharma]** **FDA converts Keytruda accelerated approval to full approval for TMB-H solid tumors** [FDA](http://www.fda.gov/drugs/resources-information-approved-drugs/verified-clinical-benefit-cancer-accelerated-approvals)
  - FDA granted traditional approval to pembrolizumab (Keytruda) on October 16, 2026, for adult and pediatric patients with unresectable or metastatic tumor mutational burden-high (TMB-H ≥ 10 mut/Mb) solid tumors.
  - Conversion fulfills post-marketing requirements following confirmatory clinical trials verifying long-term benefit.

- **FDA approves nonprescription apraclonidine eye drop Brytly for ocular redness** [FDA](http://www.fda.gov/drugs/drug-alerts-and-statements/fda-approves-new-nonprescription-eye-drop-relief-eye-redness)
  - FDA approved Brytly (apraclonidine ophthalmic solution, 0.125%), marking the first over-the-counter formulation of the α₂-adrenergic agonist for relieving minor eye redness.
  - Lower concentration delivers selective vasoconstriction without requiring a prescription.

- **FDA launches Expedited IND Pilot Program to accelerate FIH trial timelines** [FDA](http://www.fda.gov/industry/fda-actions-accelerate-and-modernize-early-and-late-stage-clinical-development/fda-expedited-investigational-new-drug-ind-pilot-program)
  - FDA unveiled the Expedited IND Pilot Program under HHS Operation TrialBlazer, accepting applications over a 45-day window to select 8–10 sponsor-institution pairs.
  - Program introduces rolling pre-IND submission reviews for pharmacology, toxicology, CMC, and clinical protocols via designated Qualified Research Institutions (QRIs) to accelerate first-in-human trial starts.

- **FDA warns of contaminated counterfeit over-the-counter eye drops** [FDA](http://www.fda.gov/drugs/counterfeit-medicine/counterfeit-versions-eye-drops-found-several-states)
  - FDA issued a public health warning regarding illegal, counterfeit OTC eye drops (including falsified *Colirio Ocusan Fast Redness Relief*) identified in Florida and Georgia retail stores.
  - Samples tested positive for bacterial contamination, posing severe risks of ocular infection and vision impairment.

- **[Big Pharma]** **FDA OPDP issues promotional untitled letters to multiple drugmakers** [FDA](http://www.fda.gov/drugs/warning-letters-and-notice-violation-letters-pharmaceutical-companies/untitled-letters)
  - Office of Prescription Drug Promotion released untitled letters targeting non-compliant promotional material across several commercial products:
  - **[Biotech]** Evolus for Jeuveau (prabotulinumtoxinA-xvfs).
  - Alar Pharmaceuticals for ALA-3000 (ketamine pamoate).
  - **[Biotech]** Travere Therapeutics for Filspari (sparsentan).
  - **[Big Pharma]** Sanofi Vaccines for Beyfortus (nirsevimab-alip).
  - **[Big Pharma]** Viatris for Tobi Podhaler (tobramycin).
  - **[Big Pharma]** Lundbeck for Vyepti (eptinezumab-jjmr).
  - Pinnacle Biologics for Photofrin (porfimer sodium).

- **FDA formally expands approved active ingredients for sunscreens** [FDA](http://www.fda.gov/drugs/understanding-over-counter-medicines/sunscreen-how-help-protect-your-skin-sun)
  - FDA updated its nonprescription sunscreen drug monograph to include broad-spectrum UV filter bemotrizinol as a permitted active ingredient.

## Business & Strategy

- **[Biotech]** **Iambic Therapeutics raises $150M in public market debut** [BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/Iambic-ipo-tom-miller-ai-drug-development-discovery/833238/)
  - Clinical-stage AI drug discovery platform Iambic Therapeutics completed a $150 million IPO, with shares surging over 50% to ~$24.50 in early trading.
  - Capital injection follows prior private backing from Abingworth, Nexus, and Catalio, contrasting with valuation declines observed across AI sector peers Recursion and Exscientia.

- **[Biotech]** **Moderna rallies on Phase 3 success for personalized cancer vaccine with Merck** [BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/biotech-charts-moderna-stock-xbi-roche-china/832886/)
  - Moderna equity experienced a multi-month rebound following landmark Phase 3 efficacy results for intismeran autogene (mRNA-4157), an individualized neoantigen therapy co-developed with Merck & Co. **[Big Pharma]** in high-risk melanoma.
  - Rebound marks a structural shift following post-pandemic revenue declines and pipeline restructuring.

## Public Health & Policy

- **HHS moves forward with peptide compounding allowance under federal plan** [STAT+](https://www.statnews.com/pharmalot/2026/10/16/hhs-peptide-push-trump-pharma-stock-holdings/?utm_campaign=rss)
  - Federal health officials are advancing regulatory frameworks to permit compounding pharmacies to prepare specific therapeutic peptides under state oversight.

- **Machine learning model uncovers extensive under-reported Valley fever incidence across US** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.10.14.26365564)
  - Multisource integration of EHR diagnoses, veterinary canine serology, and socioecological data mapped county-level *Coccidioides* fungal infection risk from 2013 to 2023.
  - Identified 60 non-reporting US counties with significant unmonitored coccidioidomycosis transmission outside traditional endemic zones.

- **Surveillance data reveals spatial shift in US measles transmission dynamics** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.10.14.26365590)
  - Analysis of US county-level measles data (2011–2025) demonstrates a shift from isolated, single-county outbreaks (2011–2020) to multi-county, sustained community transmission (2021–2025).
  - Outbreak magnitude and inter-county spread correlate strongly with declining local pediatric vaccination rates.

- **Epidemiological model evaluates age-targeted dengue vaccination strategy in Brazil** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.10.15.26365586)
  - SIR transmission model incorporating state- and age-specific seroprevalence mapped disease burden following Brazil's 2024 dengue outbreak.
  - Under restricted vaccine supply, prioritizing pediatric cohorts maximized total DALY reduction, whereas targeting older adults optimized direct mortality reduction.

***

**Worth watching:** The post-treatment attenuation observed in the Phase 3 LITESPARK-022 re-analysis (belzutifan + pembrolizumab in RCC) highlights growing regulatory and trial design scrutiny surrounding whether 1-year adjuvant targeted therapy regimens confer persistent overall survival benefits or merely delay disease recurrence while on-treatment.

- Biology & Health
    - [Two Doctors Aren’t Enough to Prove Your AI Works](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/0yHM5_7Qzw0) -- Digital Health Inside Out
        - Allon Bloch highlights the critical need for rigorous real-world testing of healthcare AI systems.
        - Merely having a functional AI model is insufficient for proving clinical effectiveness.
        - Endorsements from a small number of clinicians cannot replace comprehensive clinical validation.
    - [Can Too Much Human Oversight Ruin AI?](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/VB2gJ5iyHS4) -- Digital Health Inside Out
        - Sergei Polevikov addresses the challenge of finding the right balance between human oversight and AI automation.
        - Excessive human intervention risks negating the fundamental purpose and advantages of deploying AI.
        - Human-in-the-loop systems must be carefully calibrated so oversight does not undermine automated performance.
- Pure Science
    - [17 - Contraption #mathctober](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/IlzNThV_qcM) -- El Jj
        - The video examines the early foundations of computer science approximately a century after Ada Lovelace's contributions.
        - It explores Alan Turing and his theoretical machines as key elements in the development of early computing.
        - It continues tracing the historical and theoretical premises that led to modern computer systems.
